title: Who Killed Princess Diana? (Full Documentary)
fullText: It's 1995. Princess Diana, the most beloved woman of the decade, sits down for a BBC interview. In it, she drops a bombshell. Her husband, Prince Charles, is not fit to be king of the United Kingdom. Just 2 years later, Diana dies in a tragic car accident. And just like that, the rumors begin. Was it really an accident, or was she silenced on purpose? For the British people, it was a gut punch. They adored their princess. She was one of them. She stood by the sick, showed her emotions openly, and spoke uncomfortable truths without fear. But the royal family, they weren't fans of that. Her marriage to Charles started out like a fairy tale. A stunning dress, thousands of guests, a royal carriage. But how did that fairy tale turn into a nightmare? One that ended in the princess's death? Today, I'll break it all down. I'll tell the story of Princess Diana like it all happened yesterday. You might think Diana was just a regular girl who somehow became a princess, but that's not the full story. She came from one of Britain's oldest and most elite families, the noble house of Spencer. And just to give you an idea, the UK's most legendary prime minister, Winston Churchill, yeah, he was a Spencer, too. So, when Diana's parents, Francis Roach and John Spencer, got married in 1954, the wedding was called the event of the year. Even Queen Elizabeth II was on the guest list, along with pretty much the entire British elite. But the marriage, it was a disaster from the start. Back then, British aristocrats didn't marry for love. They married to maintain status. Diana's parents just didn't love each other. But their families still expected them to produce an heir. First, Francis and John had two daughters, Sarah and Jane. Then came a son, but tragically, he died just hours after birth. That loss only deepened the cracks in their relationship. But the pressure to have a boy didn't go away. On July 1st, 1961, their fourth child was born, another girl. They named her Diana. Her parents disappointed. The tension in the house got worse. They argued constantly and John Spencer began physically abusing his wife. Later, Francis became pregnant again and finally gave birth to a son. But by then, it was too late. The marriage was already broken. Francis fell in love with another man and in 1967 she divorced John Spencer. At the time Diana was just 7 years old. Her father went to court fighting to get custody of the children. Meanwhile, her mother left for Scotland with a new husband. Diana, her sisters, and their little brother were left behind, all on their own. Their father was always working and hardly ever home. This went on for years. In 1973, Diana was enrolled in an elite all girls [music] boarding school called West Heath. But when it came to academics, things didn't go too well. Not that anyone really cared. That school wasn't about building careers. It was about grooming girls to become proper aristocratic ladies. So, no one pushed Diana to study harder. What the teachers did remember about her, though, was the drama. Constantly crying, breaking the rules. She stood out for all the wrong reasons. And it all came down to one thing. She barely saw her parents. Even on weekends, her father hardly ever brought her home. Around that time, he became an Earl and remarried. The children instantly hated his new wife, Countess Rain Mccorquidale. They didn't even give her a chance, just nicknamed her acid rain from day one. Life wasn't easy for Diana. To escape from all the chaos, she threw herself into ballet, her absolute favorite, or got lost in a cheap romance novel. And those novels, they were all the same. Some ordinary girl meets a prince and they live happily ever after. The more she read, the more she drifted away from school work. She failed her final exams twice and never earned a high school diploma. Her father then sent her off to Switzerland to a place called the Alpine Institute. But school there didn't get any better. She was homesick, overwhelmed, and again flunked her exams. Eventually, she came back to Britain, and that was the end of her education. When Diana turns 18, her mom gives her an apartment right in the heart of London. She moves out of her father's place and starts living there with her girlfriends. At the same time, she begins looking for a job, but not because she needs the money. The Spencers never had money problems. She's job hunting because back then it was kind of a tradition for daughters of British aristocrats. Before marrying well, you were expected to work a regular job for a few years. That's when Diana starts trying out all sorts of professions. She works as a cleaner, helps out as a nanny for family friends, and even becomes an assistant teacher to a preschool. In every other way, Diana's life seemed pretty much set in stone. work a few years, marry into a good family, have kids, and spend the rest of your life running the household, just like her mother did. And that's exactly how things probably would have turned out if one day she hadn't caught the attention of none other than Queen Elizabeth II herself. Queen Elizabeth II was on the hunt for a suitable match for her eldest son, Prince Charles. He was destined to be the next king of the United Kingdom and the future stability of the entire country rested on him. So picking a wife for him was no casual affair. At this time Charles was just over 30. He was the most eligible bachelor in Europe, a Cambridge graduate, a former naval officer, well read and extremely wealthy. Every time he dated a woman, the newspapers immediately dubbed her the future princess. But in reality, Charles wasn't in a rush to get married. In one interview, he made it clear that for him, marriage wasn't a love story. It was a duty to the country. My future wife will have to get used to being in my shadow, always a few steps behind me. After that, not many women were lining up to marry a prince, and the requirements were intense. She had to be of noble birth, an Anglican, and most importantly, a virgin. During the sexual revolution and the widespread use of birth control, finding a candidate who met all those criteria, even among aristocrats, was nearly impossible. And Charles himself wasn't exactly motivated to find someone. Everyone knew about his romance with Camila Shand. The problem, he couldn't marry her. Everyone considered her unsuitable for a prince. She came from a lower social background and didn't have the best reputation. Charles and Camila first met back in the 70s. At first, their relationship was seen just as a casual fling, but the queen wasn't a fan of this little romance. Prince Charles gets sent off to serve in the Navy, and Camila is married off. For a while, that seems to calm things down. But when Charles returned from his service, he started seeing Camila again, and the press quickly caught wind of it. Photos surfaced of Camila and Charles spending time together. It caused a real scandal. The British public weren't happy and the royal family's approval rating took a hit. To fix the situation, the search for a proper bride for the prince begins. That's when Queen Elizabeth starts looking at the Spencer family. Charles is introduced to Diana's older sister, Sarah. In 1977, the prince visits their family estate, but it soon becomes clear that Sarah isn't interested in becoming a princess. She openly says she won't live by royal rules. And just like that, their relationship ends. So the queen decides Diana would make a better match for her son. Starting in the summer of 1980, Diana is invited to various events where Charles would be present. At one of those events, they get to know each other better. Diana is 19, Charles is 32, and everything goes smoothly. She's even invited to Balmer, the Queen's family estate in Scotland. There she meets the entire royal family for the first time. During this visit, Diana laughs at Charles jokes, goes fishing with him, and even joins him on hunting trips. Because of this, both the queen and the prince take a liking to her. Soon, Diana genuinely falls for Charles and eagerly looks forward to every new meeting. She adjusts her schedule to match with the busy life of the prince. And while he's tied up with official duties, she waits for a call from his secretary to set up their next rendevous. The press quickly catches on to the prince's new companion. Dozens of photographers track down where she lives and starts waiting outside her apartment. One goes even further, showing up at the preschool where Diana works. He asks for permission to photograph her with the children outside. At just the right moment, the sun peaks out, lighting up Diana's thin skirt and highlighting her long legs. Within hours, the photo is in every newspaper. When Charles sees it, he tells Diana, "I always knew you had beautiful legs, but I never imagined just how stunning they are." The photo becomes iconic. Diana starts being compared to Marilyn Monroe because just like Marilyn's famous photo, everyone can't stop talking about her legs. The British public starts falling for Diana and the press can't get enough. They want more stories, more photos. But the royal communications team isn't thrilled about that one photo. They worry it could damage the image of a future princess. So, the press office begins monitoring Diana's every move. Any potentially controversial photos are bought up and destroyed. The world is supposed to see Diana not as a new sex symbol, but as a modest young woman, the perfect [music] bride for the prince. And while Diana truly was the perfect match for Charles, he wasn't in a hurry to propose. This begins to frustrate the royal family. So Charles's father sends him a blunt message. Either marry this girl or let her go. Charles takes his father's note as an order. On February 6th, 1981, at Windsor Castle, he proposes to Diana. At first, she laughs, thinking it's a joke, but when she realizes he's serious, she says yes. On February 24th, the royal family officially announces the engagement of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer. By that point, they'd only met about 13 times. So, The Prince and the Princess Fairy Tale begins, but it started with a pretty awkward moment. Just a week after the proposal, journalists caught up with Charles and Diana for an interview. And I suppose in love, of course. Whatever in love mean. [clears throat] Diana wasn't expecting that answer. Turns out Charles didn't actually love her. And honestly, that's not surprising. At that point, they barely even know each other. Plus, they were just too different. Charles grew up in a golden cage with endless duties as a prince. He spent his entire childhood seeing his mother only at official events. And instead of hugging Diana, he'd shake her hand formally. He never even went to a regular school. His parents sent him to a strict Scottish boarding school and later to Cambridge. See, Charles loved reading philosophy, while Diana devoured romance novels. The prince could easily discuss art or politics. Diana, on the other hand, was terrified of public speaking and joked that her brain was the size of a pee. In short, they were living in completely different worlds. [music] And that's not even mentioning the age gap. But after the engagement was announced, the whole world started counting down to their wedding. It was scheduled just 4 months later. And during that time, Diana's romantic dreams completely crumbled. When she officially became the fiance of the prince of the United Kingdom, she quit her job and moved into the royal residence at Clarence House. That same day, a guard told her, "This is the last evening of your normal life. Enjoy it." And as Diana herself said after that, she wandered through empty rooms for hours. No one greeted her. No one explained anything. Though another version says that that evening she was actually met by both the queen and Charles. One thing is certain, nobody taught Diana how to be a princess. Sure, she came from an aristocratic family, but the royal family is a whole different world. After the engagement, Diana was completely lost. At her first official reception, she didn't even know which hand to hold her purse in. After some time, she was moved to the royal family's main residence, Buckingham Palace. It's somewhere between a luxurious home and the Queen's office, and things only got worse there. Diana was given her own separate room where she felt lonely and scared Charles wasn't around. To distract herself, Diana began to eat a lot. From childhood, she had a tendency to overeat and carried a bit of extra weight, something Diana openly talked about herself. Over time, this escalated [music] into bulimia. At Buckingham Palace, she'd often sneak to the kitchen. Staff reported that at night, Diana would eat large amounts of sweets. Afterwards, she would make herself sick because she feared gaining weight. Her bulimia worsened when Charles hugged her around the waist and remarked that she was a little chubby. After that, she began losing weight very quickly. By the time of her wedding, her waist had shrunk by 10 cm, which is almost 4 in. Everything got worse with the constant stress. Diana started to realize that her life was about to change completely. She hoped Charles would somehow support her, but he didn't. As if that wasn't enough, around the same time, Diana discovered Charles's old romance with Camila. She asks him about it directly. Charles admits that he did love Camila once, but it's all in the past. They're just friends now. Diana doesn't buy it. She starts getting jealous, secretly checking his mail and constantly suspecting him of cheating. And right before the wedding, she finds a gold bracelet that Charles had ordered for Camila. It's engraved with intertwining letters G and F. Diana asks what it means, and the prince says it's just a gift for a friend. GF stands for Girl Friday, a nickname they used for Camila. But Diana believes her own version that GF actually means Glattis and Fred, secret names Charles and Camila had for each other during their romance. With just one day to go before the wedding, Diana is like a girl on a roller coaster, laughing one minute, crying for hours the next, she feels like Charles doesn't care about her feelings at all. But the prince's friends said he simply didn't know how to comfort her. He grew up in a family where no one ever showed emotions. And now this wildly emotional girl shows up in his life. The bracelet story completely breaks Diana. She tells her sisters, "I can't marry Charles." But their response, "Sorry love, your face is already on every tea towel in the country." Tea towels are one of the Brits's favorite souvenirs. Calling off a royal wedding, not going to happen. The truth is, Diana was adored by the public, and that was what really mattered. The Queen's PR team was banking on this wedding to give the monarchy a muchneeded boost. They declared it a national holiday, a perfect distraction from everything else going wrong. In the early8s, the UK was going through tough times. Unemployment was high. The economy was a mess. The younger generation started protesting, blaming the government and the queen. People began to wonder, do we even need a monarchy anymore? And if on top of all that, the prince's wedding got cancelled. Yeah, that would have been a total disaster. So on July 29th, 1981, the royal wedding does happen. 3,500 of the most influential people gather inside St. Paul's Cathedral in London. 28 million people across Britain tune in to watch it live on TV. Another 750 million watch it around the globe. The lavish wedding costs the country £3 million and it's worth every penny. To the average Brit, Diana becomes the real deal, a modern-day Cinderella. Just a regular girl who became a princess. Just yesterday, nobody really knew her. And today, she's riding through London in a golden carriage. And that image alone is what saves the reputation of the British monarchy. Diana truly believed that after the wedding, Charles would finally forget about Camila and start focusing on her. That's the hope she carried with her into their honeymoon. The couple set off on a cruise aboard the royal yacht Britannia. For the first time ever, the prince [music] and the princess were truly alone together. And that's when it became painfully clear. They had absolutely nothing to talk about. Charles, as I mentioned earlier, was deep into philosophy. And out of sheer boredom, he suggested they read a book by his favorite author together. According to Diana, that was the low point of the entire honeymoon. But there's another version of events. This one from the staff aboard the yacht. They say the couple actually had a great time and looked genuinely happy together. So maybe Diana made up the story about the book. Who knows? After the honeymoon, they moved into Kensington Palace. But Charles, he rarely stayed the night. In fact, during the cruise, just days after the wedding, he called Camila for the first time. He kept telling Diana they were just friends. Diana didn't believe him again. And all of this pushed her deeper into depression and triggered a battle with bulimia. Things started to get better when Diana found out she was pregnant. She became the first woman in British royal history to give birth not in a palace, but in a regular hospital. On June 21st, 1982, Prince William was born. That brought Diana and Charles closer, at least for a while. About a year later, the couple took on their first major international tour to Australia and New Zealand. But this wasn't a honeymoon. It was official business. Britain had once been a massive empire, but by the 1980s, that empire had crumbled. Some of the former colonies had chosen to join the Commonwealth, which meant Queen Elizabeth II was still technically their monarch, but these countries were now fully independent with their own governments. Australia was one of those countries and more and more people there were questioning why they even needed a monarchy anymore. So the royal visit from the prince and princess, [music] it was meant to change their minds. When Diana and Charles arrived in Australia, huge crowds greeted them in every city. Local newspapers printed glowing pictures of the smiling couple. Diana brought little William along and insisted on caring for him herself, something unheard of at the time. Her charisma, openness, and authenticity were magnetic. People trusted her. In most photos, she looked like a joyful fairy tale princess. But some pictures told a [music] different story. Diana in tears. The tour was brutal [music] for her. Sweltering heat, endless events, and having to smile non-stop for the cameras. When the prince and princess stepped out of the car, the crowd started chanting one name, Diana. They weren't there for Charles. People were shouting for him to bring out his wife. Charles tried to laugh it off, joking. Can you really tell a woman what to do these days? But behind the smile, he was stunned. This was supposed to be his moment. He was the future king, the one everyone should have been looking at. He always said that his wife would walk behind him. But now that was clearly no longer the case. And yet, despite the awkwardness, something incredible happened. Australians started changing their minds. They began to support keeping the monarchy. And let's be honest, it wasn't because of Charles. It was because of Diana. This was the moment Diana realized her own power. In just a few short months, the shy, quiet girl transformed into a global star. And the media, they couldn't get enough of her. [music] They noticed that whenever Diana's face was on the front page, sales skyrocketed. So what did they do? They doubled down and started chasing her even harder. At the time there were over 10 national newspapers in the UK, and that's not even counting local ones. Every single day, Brits were buying 20 million copies. So naturally, the competition got fierce. Every newspaper [music] wanted more readers. Everyone was hunting for the next big headline. The Daily Tabloids were the most ruthless, drawing people in with gossip, scandals, and anything juicy about aristocrats. But here's the thing, the royal family, they were kind [music] of boring. Nothing dramatic ever happened, so the press mostly left them alone. But then along came a media gold mine, Diana. A princess who wasn't afraid to show emotion, who actually loved talking to people, and that made her nothing like Charles. Always distant, always reserved. In 1984, the prince and princess welcomed their second son, Harry. But soon after Harry's birth, things between Charles and Diana started to fall apart. She stayed in Kensington Palace with the kids, and Charles, he moved out to his countryside estate, High Grove. And guess what? That estate just happened to be 10 minutes away from Camila's house. Total coincidence, right? Now, it was very convenient for Charles to pop by and see his old friend. Oh, and fun fact, Camila's husband was cheating on her, too. So, everyone was pretty okay with the arrangement. Everyone except Diana. Trying to cope with everything going on, Diana poured herself into motherhood. To the British public, she wasn't just the honest, relatable princess anymore. She was now a devoted mom, too. Traditionally, royal children were raised almost entirely by nannies. But not Diana. She was hands. She spent every free moment with her boys. She played with them, picked them up from school, even brought them along on official trips. She accused Charles of not caring enough, of pushing all parental duties onto her. But to be fair, Charles was the heir to the throne. His life was packed with royal duties. Spending long stretches of time with the kids just wasn't an option. Once their eldest son, William, was playing golf when he got hit in the head with a club. He was rushed to the hospital. Both Charles and Diana went there immediately. Doctors said William needed surgery on his skull. Nothing too serious, but still in operation. Diana, of course, stayed with her son. But Charles had a major meeting scheduled with European environmental leaders. Environmental causes were a huge part of his life's work, and he chose to attend the meeting. The press hated that. Newspapers slammed him as a bad father. But here's the truth. Charles called the hospital constantly. He made sure William was okay and he knew the surgery wasn't critical. Charles did love his children, but like the rest of the royal family, he just wasn't raised to show emotion in public. And if he was a good father, well, as a husband, he definitely wasn't. Because around that time, he starts spending more and more time with Camila. Diana tries everything she can to save her marriage. On Charles's 37th birthday, she plans a special surprise for him. They go together to a classical opera concert, one of Charles's favorites. And in the middle of the performance, Diana actually steps onto the stage and starts dancing. The audience loves it. Charles, not so much. That same year, Diana and Charles attend a big charity concert together. Nearly every big star of the time is performing. Freddy Mercury, David Bowie, Sting, and many others. Charles dismissed it as some pop concert dragged on him by his wife. But for Diana, it was pure magic. She loved the music and knew many of these global stars personally. She was friends with Elton John, danced with John Travolta at a White House reception, and absolutely adored Michael Jackson. Once Michael came to London for a concert, and the organizers asked him not to perform his then popular song, Dirty Diana, worried it might offend the princess. But after the show, Diana herself approached Jackson and said, "Why didn't you sing that song? It's my favorite." People admired Diana. She was a style icon. Anything she wore would sell out instantly in stores. She even started wearing what was considered men's clothing at the time. [music] Loose blazers, jumpers, jackets, and millions of women around the world copied her style. Soon, Diana started dedicating herself to charity. The royal family handled charity work too, but it was very formal, following protocols and often without any sort of personal involvement. Diana, however, showed the British public real human compassion and not just for the cameras. Sometimes she even took her sons with her and secretly visited terminally ill patients to show them a different side of life. Her boldest act came in 1987. At the time, there was a major campaign against AIDS, a disease considered the plague of the 20th century. People were terrified, believing that they could catch it through touch. And in April, Diana visited Britain's first hospital for AIDS patients. She removed her gloves and shook a patient's hand. This convinced the public that simply touching someone wouldn't infect them. A People magazine reporter called it the best thing the British monarchy had done in 200 years. Diana's popularity soared to 45%, just 1% shy of the queen herself. The newspapers kept printing those happy photos of the prince and the princess, but in reality, their marriage existed only on paper. Queen Elizabeth II didn't approve of her son's romance with Camila. But she wasn't about to interfere in his [music] personal life. Diana had no choice but to accept things as they were. But she decided if her husband could cheat, why couldn't she? And so Diana's love life took off. It started with her bodyguard, Barry Manaki. He was 14 years older than Diana and married. When the affair came to light, he was fired. A year later, he died in a car crash. Some claimed it was a British intelligence operation. [music] In reality, he was just riding on the passenger seat of a motorcycle that collided [music] with a car driven by a 17-year-old inexperienced driver. Besides, Diana had other lovers who lived quietly after their affairs with her. One of those was James Hwitt, a cavalry officer and Diana's riding instructor. Their romance lasted four years and sparked rumors that Huitt was Prince Harry's real father. Why? Because they were both redheads. But that was impossible. Harry was born in 1984, and the affair didn't start until two years later. His red hair was purely genetic. Diana's older sister, Sarah, also had red hair. In short, people knew far more about Diana's affairs than Charles's. That's because the press never stopped watching her. At first, she enjoyed the attention, but over time, it started to irritate her. This became especially clear as Prince Harry and Prince William grew older. Photographers would chase Diana while she was walking with her sons. She begged them not to follow or scare the kids, but they didn't listen. That's when Diana came up with a way to get back at the press. The princess started wearing the same outfit for several days in a row. Papers paid less for those photos since it looked like they'd been taken on the same day. Then Diana took it a step further. She deliberately exited cars with her back to the cameras so no one could capture her face. And that was just the beginning. Soon, Diana started using the press to her advantage. She would accidentally leak info to the journalists about her upcoming trips, and she timed these trips right after Charles's important meetings. Diana knew that any news about her would overshadow her husband's headlines. In February 1992, Diana and Charles went on a visit to India. There, the princess asked the photographers to snap a picture of her sitting alone on a bench near the Taj Mahal, the classic spot where couples traditionally posed. Diana explained that Charles had promised to come with her, but at the last minute, he left her alone to attend a business meeting. The next day, newspapers ran the photo with the headline, "I wish you were here with me." During that same visit, another awkward moment happened. The royal photographer wanted to capture a kiss between the prince and the princess. Charles leaned in towards Diana, but she turned away at the last second. The result was a weird photo of Charles awkwardly kissing Diana's neck. Journalists had a field day. Charles forgot how to kiss his wife. By 1992, everyone already knew that Charles and Diana's marriage was in trouble. But no one knew the full story until May of that year when journalist Andrew Morton released his book Diana, her true story. [music] The world finally got the inside scoop on life in the palace. Diana's battle with bulimia, her suicide attempts, and Charles long affair with Camila. The royal press office claimed Diana had nothing to do with it. Morton was labeled a liar, and the book was dismissed as servant gossip. Diana, however, confirmed that she had never actually met or spoken with [music] Morton, and it was true. She never met him in person. Instead, she recorded answers to her prepared questions on a tape recorder and passed the tapes to Morton through a friend. At the time, nobody knew this. Still, Diana feared that her secret would soon be discovered, and she was convinced that British intelligence was constantly watching her, and she wasn't wrong to be worried. In August 1992, The Sun publishes a recording of a phone call between Diana and her friend James Gilby. Supposedly, the call was accidentally intercepted by a radio hobbyist. [music] In it, the princess vents about the royal family and Charles himself. Gilby affectionately calls Diana Squidgy, meaning soft or vulnerable. That's how the scandal came to be known as Squidgate, a nod to the Watergate scandal in the US. Later, it turns out the call wasn't intercepted by accident. They were actually eavesdropping on Diana on purpose. The goal was to get her to admit she'd been the source leaking information to Morton the whole time. After this, the royal family stops speaking to Diana, and Prince Charles's popularity takes a nose dive. The following year, British papers leak a recording of the prince himself, this time talking to Camila. The scandal is dubbed Camila Gate. The call sounded like a phone sex conversation. Charles tells Camila he wishes he could be her tampon. This earns him the nickname Mr. tea. After all this, trying to show the public a picture of a happy family was pointless. British Prime Minister John Major announces in Parliament that the couple is separating amicably, but not divorcing. They weren't allowed to divorce. They had duties to the state they were expected to fulfill. Still, journalists kept fueling the story. In 1994, Charles gives a 2-hour interview to the BBC. Everyone's waiting to hear what he'll say about Diana and Camila. He asks, "Were you faithful to your wife?" And Charles responds, "Yes, while it still meant something." For the first time, a member of the royal family publicly admits to cheating. On the day that interview airs, Diana [music] appears in public wearing a revealing dress. Journalists call it the revenge dress. A year later, she gives her own BBC interview, repeating everything Morton had written. Diana looks shattered and scared. She says she's constantly being watched and that the royal family doesn't love her because she acts with her heart, not her head. And when asked about Camila, she says there were three of us in this marriage and I don't like crowds. But what everyone talked about most were Diana's words about Charles. She says she doesn't see him as the future king and that she doesn't want to be queen of this country. She wants to be the queen of people's hearts. Her interview is watched by 23 million Brits at the same time. Diana's popularity soarses. Her approval rating hits 92% even higher than Queen Elizabeth II. A month later, the Queen sends a letter to Charles and Diana advising them to divorce. That's how their marriage comes to an end. Six months of negotiations over divorce terms begin and on August 28th, 1996, the couple finally officially separates. Diana receives £17 million in compensation and retains the right to continue living in Kensington Palace. Custody of the children is shared equally, but all major decisions about their future are to be made solely by the royal family. After all, Prince William is the future king. Diana loses the title her royal highness and keeps only Princess of Wales. This meant she now had to bow to Prince Charles and even her own children. But Diana was fine with that because she was finally free. For the first time in 15 years, the princess can live life on her own terms. She focuses on charity work, helping the homeless, people with AIDS, cancer, and leprosy. She also supports the English National Ballet, which she has adored since childhood. In early 1997, the Red Cross invites her to back [music] a campaign to ban landmines. Diana agrees and travels to Angola, where a civil war has been raging for 20 years. The British government opposes the trip. It's dangerous, but nothing stops her. In Angola, a population of 13 million faced 70 million landmines. about five mines per person. The country is full of men, women, and children maimed by explosives. Diana brings a BBC film crew, dons a bulletproof vest and protective mask, [music] and walks across a freshly cleared minefield. It's risky. Just days earlier, children had been killed on what was supposedly a cleared area. And Diana's courageous act pays off. By December 1997, 122 countries, including the UK, sign a treaty banning landmines. In 1996 to 1997, Diana makes two trips to Pakistan. Officially, it's to help raise funds for a local cancer center. But there's another reason. Even before her divorce in London, she met a heart surgeon named Huznut Khan, who had come from Pakistan. Diana spends a lot of time at the hospital where he works. She starts exploring Islam, listening to Eastern music, and wearing traditional Pakistani clothes. She heads to Pakistan to visit Khan's family, even though he doesn't even know she's coming. [music] Diana wants to keep her new relationship out of the press. But of course, the media finds out anyway. Some journalists even start spinning rumors about an engagement. And an ordinary heart surgeon just can't handle that kind of attention. He doesn't want to sacrifice his private life. And soon Diana's romance with him comes to an end. The princess is heartbroken. And that's when she gets an invitation from Egyptian billionaire Muhammad Alfa to visit his estate in France. He's been trying for years to become part of the British elite. But even though he's rich, he's never fully accepted. People see him as a flashy businessman. So Muhammad hatches a plan to gain influence through Diana. First, he befriends her stepmother, then invites Diana and her kids to vacation on the French Riviera. And coincidentally, his son, Dodi Alfa, happens to be there, too. He's not a very successful film producer and always relies on his father's help. Muhammad decides that a marriage between his son and Diana could open doors to the top tiers of British society. Sure enough, a romance sparks between Diana and Dodi, and the princess even tips off the press about where they can be photographed together. Soon, newspapers are full of photos showing Diana relaxing on a yacht with Dodi. After that, on August 30th, 1997, the couple checks into the Ritz Hotel in Paris, owned by Muhammad Aled. Around midnight, they decide to head to Dod's apartment, but outside the hotel's main entrance, photographers are waiting. The couple decides to wait for a bit, and later they leave through a back exit in a black Mercedes. Behind the wheel is the hotel's head of security, Enri Paul.
